title_q: How Do You Know Surgeries Actually Happened?
title_short: V05 · How Do You Know Surgeries Actually Happened?
headline: The skeptic's question, answered by the CEO: Watsi tracks every patient to the outcome, shows the proof on watsi.org, says what goes wrong, and lets donors choose another patient.
story: How do we know care actually happens? Many people in the Watsi community came as nonprofit skeptics, so trust and transparency have been built into the model since day one.
Every patient is tracked to the outcome, and the proof for every patient is public on watsi.org: over 35,000. When plans change, Watsi says so, and donors choose another patient.
Audits, site visits, spot checks. Not a perfect system, but the most transparent one they know how to build.

No stats graphics. The captions carry the numbers.
No title card, logo or corner bug before the end card.
Don't over-cut: rapid trims make the teleprompter read show.
No font but Lato. No second aspect ratio.
